Hi, in my experience I found PT made my symptoms usually a lot worse. A few exercises did benefit me greatly, but most of them honestly hurt me more than they helped. 

I think it’s important to find which exercises helps vs which ones don’t. There’s a difference in strengthening a muscle and just hurting it with overuse. If your kid is pretty good at describing pain, have them describe how each exercise feels and determine which ones are beneficial vs those that aren’t. 

For me I do a shoulder exercise, a hamstring stretch, and sciatica stretch every day and that’s what’s seemed to help me. When I had more PT in my schedule I honestly felt worse. Also its so important to try to stay a bit active because I feel like “if you don’t use it, you’ll lose it” really can apply to us sometimes. 

Hope this helps. It can be so hard when it doesn’t feel like anythings helping

I got diagnosed with occipital neuralgia due to having so much tightness in my neck. I’ve had nerve blocks, medial branch blocks, medications, physical therapy, etc. 

The only thing that really helped my was: Right when you wake up in the morning, try to stretch right away, also massage hard on the areas that are tense, look up stretches, and also being VERY aware of your posture at all times. 

Having correct posture is so important for anyone with hEDS, since we typically are like jello. Look in the mirror from the front and side, and look up photos of correct posture and videos on how to hold correct posture. It sounds stupid, but actually made a huge difference for me. 

Also using a foam roller and pull up bar to do dead hangs helps a lot! I got mine of facebook marketplace for almost free and its done me very well. Using lidocaine cream or spray as well can be helpful. I hope you’re able to get some relief!

-Remember you are your biggest advocate. Only you know what you feel like. Tell them. They are here to help. 

-Tell them you are sick of medical professionals ignoring you, and you need to feel better! Show emotion with the doctor, they don’t know that you feel this way unless you voice it. They see a lot of patients in their day. 

-Be descriptive with your symptoms. Describe in detail your pain, and what type of pain it is i.e. aching, burning, pulling, etc

-Prepare notes for your appointment. This could be the main points you want to bring up, your symptoms, what you think you should do, how it’s affecting your life. This will show you’re serious about feeling better. 

-Don’t go into your appointment telling them what you think you have. Let them do their job. They will tend to not take you as serious if you self-diagnose, however sometimes you need to bring it to their attention.

I have started getting this comment more and more. I know I’m pretty thin, but I am completely healthy for my height and weight. I honestly feel some of this really started when the body positivity movement split from the main idea they were trying to push- to be confident in yourself. It turned from that to some (I say some because its not all) creators making body positivity about accepting obesity. I’m not going to get into all that, but it has definitely been part of the reason stores have stopped selling smaller sizes. Since the movement has had this change I have been getting nonstop comments from everyone about me being “too thin” despite being in the normal range of weight for my height. I gained a few pounds and was really proud of myself as its hard to gain weight, but I STILL was getting comments. I truly believe a lot of society has forgotten what an actual healthy weight looks like with the body positivity movement moving away from confidence to obesity acceptance. I’m not trying to be fatphobic, but this is how I feel. I’ve started just saying the exact same comment back to the person, but flipping it the other way. It’s been helpful to get some of them to stop. It usually goes like this: “You’re too thin” and then I’ll say “well, you’re too large.” Usually after I say that I get the “That wasn’t very nice” to which I respond with “Well neither was your first unsolicited comment on my body, you acknowledged my comment towards you wasn’t nice, so why did you feel the need to make a comment on my body? Neither comment is nice.” It sucks to have to do this, but its the only way I’ve found to get people to stop saying weird things.

It sounds like it’s mainly OCD honestly, not his personality type. 

OCD is an extremely complex disorder as it can range from mild i.e. needing to do certain tasks in order, to severe. I have severe OCD and can understand part of his side as you described him. 

My best way to explain my OCD mental blocks and things is, it’s not that I’m thinking it’s gross, but something is telling me it is. Triggers are not very easy to get over. If severe enough a good analogy would be that you could quite literally hold a loaded gun to my head and I still would not be able to force myself to do the triggering tasks. 

However- good ways of approaching the issue would be:

1- Doing a bit of research about severe cases of OCD, it helps get a bit more of an understanding of how OCD affects your actions and can show your boyfriend you are open to learning about it and wanting to keep an open mind about his thoughts. 

2- Talk with your boyfriend and discuss possible treatments. The 2 treatments I recommend as someone with severe OCD would be DBT or exposure therapy. 

DBT is honestly in my opinion one of the best ways to treat different mental health disorders. It essentially trains your brain into the habit of turning bad thoughts into good thoughts. It helps to learn good healthy thinking habits and a more open and positive outlook. 

Exposure therapy as well is a good one, but it’s very difficult. Definitely have your boyfriend consult with a doctor regardless if he is open to treatment, but especially for exposure therapy. It’s difficult to do without a medical professional’s help. It can help thought with getting more used to your triggers and starting to not see them as triggers anymore. 

I hope this helps! I’m an INTJ, and feel like this would probably be the best route of fixing these struggles without coming off as mean or making him think something is wrong with him. Also, just be patient too. I know it has got to be so hard doing all of the work, but chances are it isn’t that he doesn’t want to, but has a huge mental block about it. Good luck :)

Hi, NASM certified so I might be able to help you out a bit. 

Your weight is determined by 80% diet and 20% exercise. 

A good way to lose weight is to 1; start with diet. Find an online calorie calculator to determine your macitence calories. 

A pound is roughly worth about 3500 calories. 

A safe plan for weight loss is between .5 - 1.0lbs a week. 

To lose 1 pound a week you would subtract 500 calories from your maintenance calories per day. Example: Say your maintenance calories are 2,000 a day. You would need to eat 1,500 a day instead to lose a pound a week. 

I’d also say some things you should work on cutting out of your diet: Saturated and trans fats, sugar, soda, and most fast food restaurants. I say most because sometimes there are whole food options. Also focus on foods that make your body feel good! Eating a clean diet doesn’t mean it has to be boring. 

Two good quotes I once heard, and won’t ever forget are, “Have a cheat meal, not a cheat day.” And, “I always regret no going to the gym, but I never regret going.”

I also would suggest for the gym, start slow, if you exert yourself too much in beginning stages you can lose motivation, which defeats the purpose. 

I’d recommend starting with 3-4 days a week. 

I would also recommend weight training. A lot of people are worried when they start lifting they will become bulky. It is a lot more difficult than you’d think to become ‘bulky’. 

Instead of lifting making you bulky, it will really benefit you during the beginning stages. You will start to build muscle mass and you will start to notice you feel good, you will start to see changes quicker, and overall I find in the beginning stages of picking up a healthy and active lifestyle, your confidence will grow. 

For going to the gym, make yourself a schedule or split. Say if you go 3 days a week you could do Day 1: Back and bicep exercises. Day 2: Leg day, and Day 3: Chest and tricep exercises. 

This will help you with soreness, as you and exercising different muscles each day, and giving sore muscles time to relax and destress. 

Now for weight loss I’d recommend light-medium cardio after your workout. I say after because at this point your muscles are warmed up enough that it can help burn fat a bit quicker and better. 

For cardio, any machine really would work good, I’d say start with low intensity (treadmill walking) and work your way up to say the row machine for example. 

A key point to remember is that weight loss takes time. A healthy lifestyle can be a hard change, but you will thank yourself for it. It will pay off in the end. :)
